title: Auditioning for Lucky Millinder at the Savoy
summary: Trevor Bacon recruits him; he outplays Shadow Wilson at a Savoy audition and wins the job.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And after I left there, Trevor Bacon was at the show; he caught the show, and he came backstage, and he wanted to know how long was I going to be staying with Roy Eldridge, and I asked him why, and he said that Lucky was looking for a drummer.

Well, I had heard so much about Lucky Millinder and his Blue Rhythm Ribbon Band, so I was real thrilled about him asking me this. Well, I didn't know what was gonna happen with Roy, so I told him, that "Well, I don't know what we're gonna be doing." So he said, "Look, we're rehearsing at the Sunset Ballroom", which was up on 125th Street between 8th Avenue and St. Nicholas, and so I went up there and I made a rehearsal with Lucky.

Well, I didn't know at the time that this band that Lucky was rehearsing was really Bill Doggett's band out of Philadelphia, and the drummer with the band was Shadow Wilson, and for some reason, Shadow and Lucky didn't sort of hit it off too good, so he had a gig at the Savoy Ballroom on a Sunday night, and it was sort of like an audition between Shadow and myself.

So I would play one set and then Shadow played one set, and at the end of the night Lucky told me that I had the job. Shadow was out. Also, on that same night, Mr. Buchanan who ran the Savoy Ballroom, told Lucky that he'd meet him in the morning down at Moe Gale's office because he was gonna sign him up to a contract. And we were gonna be like one of the house bands there at the Savoy -- the house band at the time was the Savoy Sultans; Erskine Hawkins and Teddy Hill -- those were the house bands at the time.
